metadata_used.title: The tide nobody can explain.
metadata_used.description:
There are two high tides a day, and only one of them makes sense.

The Moon lifts the near ocean — fine. But twelve hours later the sea rises again on the side of the planet facing away. The explanation most of us were taught for that one — centrifugal force — is named as a misconception in the physics literature. Nothing out there is being pushed.

Gravity weakens with distance. The Moon pulls the near ocean hardest, the solid Earth a little less, and the far ocean least of all. Subtract the pull on the Earth itself and what is left points outward at both ends. The planet is pulled out from under its own water.

A tide is not gravity being strong. It is gravity being uneven — which is also why your bath has no tide.

Sources:
NOAA, Gravity, Inertia and the Two Bulges · https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/education/tutorial_tides/tides03_gravity.html
Confusion around the tidal force and the centrifugal force · https://arxiv.org/pdf/1506.04085
NASA Science, Tides · https://science.nasa.gov/moon/tides/
